mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increase and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over three months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between HOUST decrease and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals labor market distress, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the immediate economic impact.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increase and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production is associated with economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO increase and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over three months signals an easing monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as lower borrowing costs stimulate economic activity.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 35% of the instances where the easing condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS decrease and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month, coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals a weakening consumer demand and labor market distress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases > 1% and UNRATE increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of RSAFS decrease and UNRATE increase on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the positive economic signal.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between PAYEMS increase and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a month, coupled with an increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5%, signals a deflationary environment with increasing supply, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real purchasing power increases.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases > 0.5% and INDPRO increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of CPIAUCSL decrease and INDPRO increase on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
